module

public import Mathlib.Topology.Defs.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

@[expose] public section

/--
A topological space `X` has Lebesgue covering dimension at most `n` if every finite
open cover of `X` admits a finite open refinement in which no point of `X` is contained
in more than `n + 1` elements.
-/
def HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (𝓤 : Set (Set X)), 𝓤.Finite → (∀ U ∈ 𝓤, IsOpen U) → ⋃₀ 𝓤 = Set.univ → ∃ 𝓥 : Set (Set X), 𝓥.Finite ∧ (∀ V ∈ 𝓥, IsOpen V) ∧ ⋃₀ 𝓥 = Set.univ ∧
  (∀ V ∈ 𝓥, ∃ U ∈ 𝓤, V ⊆ U) ∧ ∀ x : X, {V ∈ 𝓥 | x ∈ V}.encard ≤ (n + 1 : ℕ)

/--
A topological space `X` has Lebesgue covering dimension exactly `n` if it has covering
dimension at most `n` but not at most `n - 1`.
-/
def HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X n ∧ ∀ m, m < n → ¬ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X m

findings.description: The definition incorrectly assigns exact covering dimension 0 to the empty space. At n = 0, `∀ m : ℕ, m < n → ¬ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X m` is vacuous, so this predicate reduces to `HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X 0`. Every empty space satisfies that upper bound: the empty family is a finite open refinement of every cover and covers the empty space. I proved `HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq Empty 0` in `/workspace/review/boundaries.lean`. The missing lower-dimensional case is dimension −1, which the natural-number quantifier cannot test. There is no `Nonempty X` restriction.
findings.source_evidence: Engelking, Dimension Theory (1978), Definition 1.6.7 and the following paragraph, p. 54, explicitly reserve −1 for the empty space: “Clearly, dim X = −1 if and only if X = ∅.” https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/engelking.pdf . Wikipedia’s “Lebesgue covering dimension,” Examples, likewise states: “The empty set has covering dimension −1.” https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebesgue_covering_dimension
findings.suggested_fix: For the existing natural-number interface, define `HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq X n` as `Nonempty X ∧ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X n ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m < n → ¬ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X m`. Document the empty-space convention. Alternatively, introduce a strict-upper-bound predicate whose bound 0 characterizes empty spaces, and define exact dimension using that predicate.

reformulations.difference: The definition requires the refining open cover to be finite, whereas an equivalent standard characterization permits an arbitrary open refinement of each finite open cover.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Assign each refining set one containing member of the original finite cover. For each original member, take the union of all refining sets assigned to it. These finitely many open unions still cover the space and refine the original cover. Their pointwise multiplicity cannot exceed the original refinement’s multiplicity. This works without separation assumptions, including on empty spaces. The reverse implication simply forgets finiteness. Proved as `ReviewRefinements.finite_refinement_iff` in `/workspace/review/refinements.lean`; it also matches Engelking Proposition 1.6.9.

reformulations.difference: The cover families may contain the empty set, unlike Wikipedia’s convention that the members of an open cover are nonempty.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting empty members preserves the union, openness, finiteness, and pointwise multiplicities. Delete empty members of the input cover before applying the nonempty-members formulation; a refinement of that reduced cover still refines the original cover. Conversely, delete empty members of the output refinement. The argument also handles the empty space, where the empty family remains a cover. Proved as `ReviewNonemptyCovers.nonempty_members_iff` in `/workspace/review/nonempty_covers.lean`. Thus requiring nonempty cover members would not repair the separate exact-dimension defect.

reformulations.difference: Its current exact-dimension premise admits the empty space at n = 0, unlike the standard exact-dimension predicate. This dimension-related discrepancy does not change this particular implication.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On nonempty spaces, adding the proposed `Nonempty X` conjunct leaves the premise unchanged. On empty spaces, `Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X)` already holds for every n by `ChartedSpace.empty`. Consequently, the implication with the current premise is equivalent to the implication with the corrected premise, independently of the other hypotheses. Proved in the more general form `Review.charted_conclusion_iff` in `/workspace/review/boundaries.lean`. This establishes that the library defect does not warrant a duplicate dimension-related finding against this use site.

review.notes: Both target declarations and their sole problem use were checked. Boundary proofs cover empty spaces, a singleton, finite discrete spaces, monotonicity, and the immediate-predecessor characterization at positive indices. Finite multiplicity computations returned the expected 0, 1, and 2. All reported Lean proofs compile without `sorry` and their axiom audits contain no `sorryAx`. No existing Mathlib covering-dimension definition was found; small inductive dimension is a distinct notion. Beyond normal spaces, this file explicitly uses the all-open-cover extension recognized in Engelking’s discussion on pp. 222–223, not the alternative cozero-cover extension. The sole consumer is metrizable, so that convention distinction does not affect its dimension premise. No status discrepancy was found in the consulted Bing–Borsuk sources. All experiments stayed under /workspace/review/, and no checkout files were changed.

submission.summary: Added `Nonempty X` to the exact-dimension predicate and documented that the empty space has dimension −1. The file compiles without errors or warnings. Sandbox proofs confirm that empty spaces are excluded, nonempty cases are unchanged, and empty spaces still satisfy every nonnegative upper bound. No other checkout files were edited.

open cover of `X` admits a finite open refinement in which no point of `X` is contained

/--
A nonempty topological space `X` has Lebesgue covering dimension exactly `n` if it has
covering dimension at most `n` but not at most any smaller natural number.

The empty space has covering dimension `-1`, so it does not satisfy this predicate.
-/
def HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty X ∧ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X n ∧
    ∀ m, m < n → ¬ HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionLE X m
